properties.chose:
@ajs, 2026-10-18, after the REA clone was read (HEAD 92dadf933) together with Ghidra. He kept FOUR as intent:
(a) EVIDENCE AND LIMITATIONS ON EVERY RECOVERED CLAIM. Taken from REA's src/domain/evidence.ts (confidence observed|derived|inferred, authority, limitations, locations) and its refinement rules in javascriptApplicationEvidenceSchemas.ts: an inference must carry an explicit limitation; an observation must carry an actionable location; the top confidence is reserved for observed facts; a derived result inherits its inputs' limitations (WorkflowEvidence.ts).
(f) NEW: UNREACHED COVERAGE IS UNKNOWN, NOT ABSENT. Adopt states the coverage of what it read as complete, partial or unknown with a reason (REA src/domain/relationshipCoverage.ts; docs/tool-design.md: "Missing coverage is unknown, not absence"). What it did not reach is never written or read as "there is none". This is the per-scope form of the dropped req:adopt-says-how-much-it-got.
(d) A FEATURE-SCOPED ADOPT. Start from one literal seed (route, symbol, string, IPC channel, module, export) and recover only what is reachable from it in one direction (REA trace_application_feature, docs/javascript-application-workflows.md).
(g) NEW: PROOF MUST MATCH THE CLAIM IT CLOSES. From REA's reconstruction obligation ledger (docs/reconstruction-obligation-ledgers.md: "A green unit test cannot close a packaged-process obligation. A static-only source cannot close a runtime or process claim"). In reflow2 this is a verification rule, not adopt text: a verification's authority (static reading, unit, integration, deployed/live observation) must reach the claim's own level before it counts as verifying it. Medium.
CONSIDERED, NOT CHOSEN: (b) adopt with no source and (c) a recovery method per target. If taken up later, start with Electron/JS and database schemas, the only targets where REA recovers real components, interfaces and data models (its JavaScript Application Graph; SQLite schemas). Native binaries via Ghidra give functions, cross-references and pseudocode, but no module boundaries, and REA's own skill says to skip it for ordinary source repositories. The legal pushback still stands (only systems the person owns or is authorised to analyse).
(e) A REVIEW BEFORE WRITING stays considered: REA has no proposed→accepted step for its results (approval only for setup; a reviewed obligation needs review evidence), so it gives no new evidence for (e), and reflow2's proposed status already covers it.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-18: "can we learn anything in our augment the 'adopt' skill from https://github.com/morluto/rea ? If needed, when I get home, I can clone this repo on my local machine and we can inspect it closer".

WHAT REA IS (its README, read 2026-10-18; metadata checked with the GitHub API: MIT, TypeScript, created 2026-04-14, pushed 2026-10-18, about 321.5k stars and 81.5k forks):
- An MCP server through which an agent reverse-engineers software WITHOUT its source: native binaries (Ghidra, IDA, Hopper), JavaScript/Electron (modules, imports, routes, IPC boundaries), Android APKs, .NET assemblies, websites, firmware and SQLite databases (tables, columns, indexes, views).
- "results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion"; "See a feature you like. Understand how it works, down to the binary level."
- Focused, incremental inspection rather than whole-target disassembly; static analysis by default for JS and .NET; a provider per target type.
- Setup asks the person to "review the proposed changes, and approve them".
- Its own caution: commercial back-ends must be legally obtained and licensed.

WHAT ADOPT ALREADY KNOWS (reflow2's design):
- fact:adopt-recovers-depth-cleanly-and-cannot-recover-the-functional-carving: depth is recoverable, the functional carving is not;
- req:adopt-says-how-much-it-got: DROPPED earlier;
- dec:idea-run-adopt-on-reflow2-itself-as-a-ground-truth-test: open.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) EVIDENCE AND LIMITATIONS ON EVERY RECOVERED CLAIM. Each node adopt writes cites where it was seen (file, line, symbol), AND says what the method could not see (static only, no runtime path, generated code skipped). This is the per-claim form of the dropped "adopt says how much it got", and fits reflow2's inferred provenance.
(b) ADOPT A SYSTEM WITH NO SOURCE. When a decompiler or analysis MCP such as REA is connected, adopt can recover a design from a binary, an app, a website or a database schema the person is authorised to analyse: a vendor tool, a legacy binary, an old site. It is the same shape as pairing reflow2 with a domain tool (dec:idea-an-mcp-around-xrt-so-a-beamline-design-is-ray-traced-not-asserted).
(c) A RECOVERY METHOD PER TARGET TYPE. Adopt's steps are code-shaped today. A database schema yields a data model; a web app yields routes and interfaces; an Electron app yields IPC boundaries as seams; firmware yields regions.
(d) A FEATURE-SCOPED ADOPT. Recover one feature or capability slice ("see a feature you like") into the design, rather than the whole system at once: cheaper, and checkable by the person who knows that feature.
(e) A REVIEW BEFORE WRITING. Adopt proposes the recovered design as one batch the owner reviews and approves, before or as it lands, instead of writing then asking.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- LAW AND PERMISSION. Reverse-engineering software you do not own is bound by its licence and local law, and REA itself warns about commercial tool licences. (b) must say: only systems the person owns or is authorised to analyse (interoperability, their own legacy). reflow2 never runs a decompiler itself.
- HOW, NEVER WHY. A binary gives mechanics, never intent. Adopt already cannot recover the functional carving from source (measured), so from a binary every requirement and decision stays inferred and proposed until the owner speaks. Over-reading a decompile as intent is the risk.
- THE AGENT / REFLOW2 LINE. REA is agent tooling. Adopt is a served SKILL (guidance to the agent), so (b) and (c) are mostly skill text saying "if such a tool is connected, use it as evidence". reflow2 records the evidence and its limits.
- FEWER THINGS. (a), (d) and (e) are skill text over existing provenance and approval. (c) and (b) are larger.
- READ FROM THE README ONLY. Its result schema (how it shapes evidence and limitations) is not yet read. That is worth a closer look once the repo is cloned (Anthony offered), before building (a).

SIZE, as a finding: (a) small (skill plus existing provenance; perhaps one limitation field); (d) small; (e) small; (c) medium; (b) medium to large (a connected tool, the legal framing, new recipes).
properties.name: Adopt takes four things from REA ("Reverse Engineer Anything"): evidence and limits on every recovered claim, unreached coverage reads unknown (not absent), a feature-scoped adopt from one seed, and proof that matches the claim it closes; no-source recovery and a method per target stay considered
